sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访几位商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约

sentences.en: Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不会想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today,
sentences.zh: 今天，

sentences.en: A U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: deal to sell submarines to Australia has unleashed claims of backstabbing and betrayal from a close U.S.
sentences.zh: 向澳大利亚出售潜艇的协议引发了来自美国亲密盟友

sentences.en: ally.
sentences.zh: 关于背后捅刀和背叛的指责。

sentences.en: Estet Herndon spoke with our colleague, Mark Landler, about why, despite that, the United States is determined to press ahead with the plan.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特·赫登与我们的同事马克·兰德尔进行了交谈，探讨为什么尽管如此，美国仍决心按计划推进这一计划。

sentences.en: Wednesday, September 22nd.
sentences.zh: 9月22日，星期三。

sentences.en: Mark, I have to tell you that when I first heard about this news, about a deal with Australia, I really didn't understand the significance of it.
sentences.zh: 马克，我必须告诉你，当我第一次听到这个消息——关于与澳大利亚的协议时，我真的不明白它的重要性。

sentences.en: So can you tell me, plain and simple, what is this?
sentences.zh: 所以你能简明扼要地告诉我，这究竟是什么吗？

sentences.en: What is this deal?
sentences.zh: 这到底是一项什么协议？

sentences.en: Well, it's understandable because it's one of these things where when you first look at it, it doesn't necessarily look like that huge a deal, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是可以理解的，因为这类事情当你第一眼看的时候，它未必看起来那么重大，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a deal between Australia, the United States, and Britain to supply nuclear-powered submarines to Australia.
sentences.zh: 这是澳大利亚、美国和英国之间的一项协议，旨在向澳大利亚供应核动力潜艇。

sentences.en: But what makes it really such a landmark is that, in essence, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但真正让它成为里程碑的是，本质上美国

sentences.en: and Britain are sharing their most secret nuclear technology with another ally, Australia, to enable them to build and operate
sentences.zh: 和英国正在与另一个盟友澳大利亚分享他们最机密的核技术，以使他们能够建造和运营

sentences.en: a class of submarines that they otherwise would never have access to.
sentences.zh: 一类他们原本绝无可能接触到的潜艇。

sentences.en: And that really makes it stand out.
sentences.zh: 这正是它脱颖而出的原因。

sentences.en: So it's not only a huge deal in terms of monetary value, it's a really strategically important deal, one that sort of changes the equation, not just over the next five years,
sentences.zh: 因此，它不仅是一笔在货币价值上巨大的交易，更是一笔战略意义极其重大的交易，它某种程度上改变了局势，不仅是在未来五年内，

sentences.en: but really over the next 25, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 而是真正跨越未来25到30年。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: This is Australia being brought into a really uniquely close alliance with the United States and Britain to really face off against China in the Asia-Pacific.
sentences.zh: 这意味着澳大利亚被拉入了一个与美国和英国极其独特的紧密同盟中，以在亚太地区真正与中国对抗。

sentences.en: This is going to be the great geopolitical confrontation of the coming era.
sentences.zh: 这将是即将到来的时代里重大的地缘政治对抗。

sentences.en: And Australia is sort of lining up with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而澳大利亚正在某种程度上与美国

sentences.en: and Britain to be committed to this new, much more aggressive posture toward China.
sentences.zh: 和英国结成阵线，致力于对中国采取这种全新的、更具攻击性的姿态。

sentences.en: Wait, so these submarines that the United States entered to an agreement with to share a military technology with, with Australia, are actually for the purpose of spying on China?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以美国与之达成协议并与其分享军事技术的这些潜艇，也就是和澳大利亚合作的潜艇，实际上是为了监视中国？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, the issue here is China has become over the past 10 years in particular, a mighty naval power in its own right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，这里的问题在于，在过去十年里，中国尤其是崛起为一个名副其实的海军强国。

sentences.en: And it has shown very imperialistic ambitions in its own coastal waters and even well beyond into the Pacific, into the South China Sea.
sentences.zh: 它在自己的沿海水域，甚至更远延伸至太平洋和南海，都表现出了非常强烈的帝国主义野心。

sentences.en: They have their own very large submarine fleet.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有自己非常庞大的潜艇舰队。

sentences.en: They have their own very large naval fleet.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有自己非常庞大的海军舰队。

sentences.en: And they're really, in a sense, militarizing this entire Asia-Pacific area.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们正在使整个亚太地区军事化。

sentences.en: And so what the Australians are doing in concert with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，澳大利亚人与美国

sentences.en: and the U.K.
sentences.zh: 和英国协同行动，

sentences.en: is fielding their own class of very fast, very long range, very hard to detect submarines that can basically patrol the waters of the South China Sea and more
sentences.zh: 正在部署他们自己的一类非常快、航程非常远、极难被侦测的潜艇，这些潜艇基本上可以巡逻南海水域，更

sentences.en: broadly into the Pacific and keep an eye on the Chinese and basically watch what they're doing
sentences.zh: 广泛地巡逻太平洋，密切关注中国人的动向，并基本上观察他们在做什么，

sentences.en: and send a very powerful signal to the Chinese that they're not going to be able to expand into all of this space without someone pushing back on them.
sentences.zh: 向中国人发出一个非常强烈的信号，即如果没有人进行回击，他们是不可能扩张到所有这些空间的。

sentences.en: Okay, so that all seems like a fairly reasonable, straightforward military alliance.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以这一切看起来像是一个相当合理、直接的军事同盟。

sentences.en: The United
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: States, which has an interest in keeping tabs on China, partners with Australia around these submarines.
sentences.zh: 有兴趣密切关注中国，便围绕这些潜艇与澳大利亚展开合作。

sentences.en: So wait, why did this blow up into a controversy?
sentences.zh: 等等，那为什么这件事会演变成一场争议？

sentences.en: Well, because the French got really mad about this deal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为法国人对这笔交易非常生气。

sentences.en: There have been lies.
sentences.zh: 这里存在谎言。

sentences.en: There has been duplicity.
sentences.zh: 存在双面派作风。

sentences.en: To say the French got angry actually really understates it.
sentences.zh: 说法国人气愤其实真的是轻描淡写了。

sentences.en: The level of fury was really almost unprecedented for an ally.
sentences.zh: 这种愤怒的程度对于一个盟友来说几乎是史无前例的。

sentences.en: There has been a major break of truSt. There has been contempt.
sentences.zh: 信任受到了重创。充满着蔑视。

sentences.en: So it's not going well between us, not at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之间的关系进展不顺，一点也不顺利。

sentences.en: The French canceled this big gala that they were going to give to celebrate US French ties in Washington.
sentences.zh: 法国人取消了一个盛大的晚会，他们原本打算用这个晚会来庆祝华盛顿的美法关系。

sentences.en: They recalled their ambassadors from both Washington and the Australian capital
sentences.zh: 他们召回了驻华盛顿和澳大利亚首都

sentences.en: Canberra.
sentences.zh: 堪培拉的大使。

sentences.en: We're calling our ambassadors to show our former partner countries that we have very strong discontent, really a serious crisis between us.
sentences.zh: 我们正在召回大使，以向我们以前的伙伴国家表明我们有强烈的不满，我们之间确实存在严重的危机。

sentences.en: The French foreign minister referred to it as a stab in the back.
sentences.zh: 法国外长称之为背后捅刀。

sentences.en: I'm really angry.
sentences.zh: 我真的很生气。

sentences.en: What worries me is the behavior of the Americans.
sentences.zh: 让我担忧的是美国人的行为。

sentences.en: This unilateral, brutal, unpredictable decision looks a lot like what Mr. Trump used to do.
sentences.zh: 这种单边、粗暴、不可预测的决定看起来很像特朗普先生过去常常做的事。

sentences.en: So you're really seeing a level of vitriol that, as I said, is just about unprecedented in relations between the United States and France.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实看到了正如我所说的那种在美法关系中几乎史无前例的尖锐言辞。

sentences.en: The White House can't even secure a phone call to the
sentences.zh: 白宫甚至无法安排通往

sentences.en: Elysee Palace.
sentences.zh: 爱丽舍宫的电话。

sentences.en: The president will have a call it has yet.
sentences.zh: 总统将进行通话，但目前还没有。

sentences.en: We're still working on the scheduling of it with President Macron in the coming days.
sentences.zh: 我们仍在与马克龙总统敲定未来几天的通话日程。

sentences.en: Why exactly are they so mad?
sentences.zh: 他们到底为什么这么生气？

sentences.en: Well, because the French had their own deal with the Australians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为法国人自己和澳大利亚人有一笔交易。

sentences.en: They were going to sell them non-nuclear-powered submarines, also over a period of about 20 to 25 years.
sentences.zh: 他们原本要向澳大利亚出售非核动力潜艇，时间跨度也是在大约20到25年里。

sentences.en: And losing that deal hurts them in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 失去这笔交易在多个方面伤害了他们。

sentences.en: The first way is purely financial.
sentences.zh: 第一个方面纯粹是财务上的。

sentences.en: It's a $66 billion deal.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔660亿美元的交易。

sentences.en: It means a lot to their defense industry.
sentences.zh: 这对他们的国防工业意义重大。

sentences.en: So there's a very big economic hit.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常大的经济打击。

sentences.en: Secondly, there's the political sting of this for Emmanuel Macron, the president of France.
sentences.zh: 其次，这对法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙来说是一种政治上的刺痛。

sentences.en: He's running for re-election in six months.
sentences.zh: 他在六个月后将竞选连任。

sentences.en: And in French elections, a little bit of anti-American sentiment is not a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 在法国选举中，有一点反美情绪并不是件坏事。

sentences.en: But there's no question it's also a big humiliation for France on the global stage.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，这也是法国在国际舞台上的巨大羞辱。

sentences.en: And I think most importantly is that it changes the geopolitical environment.
sentences.zh: 我认为最重要的是，它改变了地缘政治环境。

sentences.en: The fact is that you've now got Australia standing alongside the United States and Britain in this major future conflict.
sentences.zh: 事实是，你现在看到澳大利亚在这个重大的未来冲突中与美国和英国站在一起。

sentences.en: And for France to be left on the sidelines of something that big is just something the French found extremely hard to swallow.
sentences.zh: 对于法国来说，被边缘化在如此重大的事情之外，是法国人极其难以接受的。

sentences.en: Well, given everything that you just said, it seems like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 好吧，鉴于你刚才所说的一切，看起来美国

sentences.en: should have been anticipating that France would have been upset by this move.
sentences.zh: 本应该预料到法国会对这一举动感到不满。

sentences.en: Did the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: see this coming?
sentences.zh: 预见到这一点了吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's no question that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，毫无疑问，美国

sentences.en: must have sensed that this was going to be a problem.
sentences.zh: 一定预感到这会成为一个问题。

sentences.en: Because after all, they negotiated this deal with the Australians and the Brits under a cloak of secrecy, without tipping off the French what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟，他们是在极其保密的情况下与澳大利亚人和英国人谈判这笔交易的，没有向法国人透露他们在做什么。

sentences.en: So that's not something you do when you think no one's going to get upset.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你认为没有人会生气时，你不会这么做。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, they obviously knew that when the Australians broke the news to the French that they were pulling out, that it was going to cause a problem.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们显然知道，当澳大利亚人向法国人抛出他们要退出的消息时，这会引发问题。

sentences.en: I think it is fair to say, though, that no one in Washington anticipated just how bad this was going to get how quickly.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为可以公平地说，华盛顿没有一个人预料到事情会恶化得如此之快、如此严重。

sentences.en: And you see that in the fact that the White House has been trying to arrange a telephone call between President Biden and President Macron to try to smooth this over.
sentences.zh: 从白宫一直在努力安排拜登总统和马克龙总统之间的电话交谈以试图平息此事，你就能看出这一点。

sentences.en: So I think the depth of the French reaction caught the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为法国反应的强烈程度让美国

sentences.en: off guard.
sentences.zh: 措手不及。

sentences.en: But the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但美国

sentences.en: could not have expected that the French were going to take this lying down.
sentences.zh: 不可能指望法国人会逆来顺受。

sentences.en: So on one hand, you have a level of anger that was larger than even the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，你看到了甚至超过美国

sentences.en: anticipated.
sentences.zh: 预期的愤怒程度。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, they knew they were going to be mad.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，他们知道法国人会生气。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: didn't care and still did it anyway.
sentences.zh: 并不在乎，却依然这样做了。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: Well, this kind of gets to the nub of what's changed over the past several years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这触及了过去几年发生变化的核心。

sentences.en: I think what's happened here is that the priority of competing against
sentences.zh: 我认为这里发生的事情是，与

sentences.en: China, of putting together the most powerful possible alliance to counter China's influence
sentences.zh: 中国竞争的优先级——即拼凑出最强大的联盟来遏制中国在该地区的影响力——

sentences.en: in the region, trumps America's historic sensitivities to and care for its relations with its allies in Europe and within NATO.
sentences.zh: 压倒了美国对欧洲和北约盟友关系的历来敏感和珍视。

sentences.en: And that is a major shift that is not so much just a shift of one administration to another.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的转变，与其说这是一届政府向另一届政府的转变，不如说

sentences.en: This is something that has been evolving and building over time.
sentences.zh: 这是随着时间不断演变和积累的产物。

sentences.en: And we saw it in a very dramatic way play out with the announcement of one deal and the breakup of another deal.
sentences.zh: 我们以非常戏剧性的方式看到了这一点，伴随着一项协议的宣布和另一项协议的破裂。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，去看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Mark, you said that there was a geopolitical shift that's been happening around China.
sentences.zh: 马克，你刚才说围绕中国一直在发生地缘政治转变。

sentences.en: Can you explain where that's coming from?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这是从哪里来的吗？

sentences.en: What's the origins?
sentences.zh: 它的起源是什么？

sentences.en: Well, think about where we were in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想想我们在20世纪80年代的处境。

sentences.en: You were looking really at a bipolar world.
sentences.zh: 你所面对的实际上是一个两极世界。

sentences.en: It was the
sentences.zh: 那是

sentences.en: United States and the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 美国和苏联。

sentences.en: And allied with us in that Cold War confrontation were our NATO allies.
sentences.zh: 在冷战对抗中与我们结盟的是我们的北约盟友。

sentences.en: So the transatlantic relationship was really the core element of the United States's security strategy.
sentences.zh: 因此，跨大西洋关系确实是美国安全策略的核心要素。

sentences.en: With the collapse of the Soviet Union, NATO lost its historic focus.
sentences.zh: 随着苏联的解体，北约失去了其历史焦点。

sentences.en: The alliance was built to confront this threat and that threat suddenly unraveled.
sentences.zh: 这个联盟是为了对抗这种威胁而建立的，而那个威胁突然消失了。

sentences.en: And it was replaced by a series of other threats, predominantly in the Middle EaSt. And so the United States continued to rely very heavily on these
sentences.zh: 它被一系列其他威胁所取代，主要在中东。因此，美国继续严重依赖这些

sentences.en: European allies.
sentences.zh: 欧洲盟友。

sentences.en: Then basically, in the 1990s and into the early 2000s, obviously, the big economic story was the rise of China.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上，在20世纪90年代和21世纪初，显而易见，重大的经济新闻是中国的崛起。

sentences.en: And for a long time, the American relationship with China was primarily framed around trade and economics.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，美国与中国的关系主要围绕贸易和经济展开。

sentences.en: But then over time, as China became a mightier economic player, it also became a very major military and security player.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，随着中国成为一个更强大的经济参与者，它也成为了一个非常重要的军事和安全参与者。

sentences.en: It began to build a blue water navy.
sentences.zh: 它开始建造蓝水海军。

sentences.zh: 有着几百年紧密联系的盟友采取了交易化的态度，法国可能觉得自己可以免受这种对待。

sentences.en: This is the kind of treatment you might expect of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是你可能会期望美国

sentences.en: with a small country in the Middle East or in Africa or in Latin America.
sentences.zh: 对待中东、非洲或拉丁美洲小国时采用的态度。

sentences.en: You wouldn't necessarily expect the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你未必会期望美国

sentences.en: to treat one of its oldest and closest allies this way.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式对待其最古老、最亲密的盟友之一。

sentences.en: So France is saying, you do this to other people, you don't do this to us.
sentences.zh: 所以法国在说：你对别人这么做可以，但你不能对我们这样做。

sentences.en: But you're saying that the
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，

sentences.en: United States in this moment, you know, that's not their priority.
sentences.zh: 美国在此刻，你知道的，那已经不是他们的优先事项了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that President Biden will spend a lot of time in the coming days and weeks trying to make the point that we still do care about you.
sentences.zh: 我确信拜登总统在接下来的日子和几周里会花很多时间来阐明这样一个观点：我们依然在乎你们。

sentences.en: You're still our allies.
sentences.zh: 你们依然是我们的盟友。

sentences.en: But I think it is fair to say that what the United States is saying to everybody is, in effect, you've got to choose.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，美国实际上是在对所有人说：你们必须做出选择。

sentences.en: You're either with us in this competition with China or you're not with us.
sentences.zh: 要么在这场对中国的竞争中与我们站在一起，要么不与我们站在一起。

sentences.en: And if you are with us, you're going to be willing to kind of do it our way.
sentences.zh: 如果你们与我们站在一起，你们就得愿意按照我们的方式行事。

sentences.en: And when you talk about Europe, it's a very complicated question because some countries are more inclined to line up with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当谈到欧洲时，这是一个非常复杂的问题，因为有些国家更倾向于几乎没有什么争论

sentences.en: with fairly little debate.
sentences.zh: 就与美国保持一致。

sentences.en: Other countries are somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 其他国家则处于中间立场。

sentences.en: And then there are countries like Germany that actually have very important, large commercial relationships with China that actually have a
sentences.zh: 还有像德国这样的国家，它们实际上与中国有着非常重要且庞大的商业关系，

sentences.en: somewhat different view of how to engage with China.
sentences.zh: 对于如何与中国接触，它们有着截然不同的看法。

sentences.en: And so there is the potential for a divergence of intereSt. There's a potential for some Europeans to view China differently than the
sentences.zh: 因此，存在着利益分歧的潜在可能。一些欧洲人对中国的看法可能会与

sentences.en: United States.
sentences.zh: 美国有所不同。

sentences.en: And I think the other subtext to what we've seen over the past few weeks with this deal is the United States kind of posing this question to Europe.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去几周我们从这项协议中看到的另一个潜台词是，美国向欧洲提出了这样一个问题：

sentences.en: You know, are you with us or are you not with us?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们究竟是跟我们在一起，还是不跟我们在一起？

sentences.en: And countries have to decide how much they want to line up with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 各个国家必须决定他们希望在多大程度上与美国保持一致，

sentences.en: and what they're willing to tolerate in order to be part of this effort.
sentences.zh: 以及为了成为这一努力的一部分，他们愿意容忍什么。

sentences.en: So the picture that you're painting here seems to be a world of small distinctions where the United
sentences.zh: 所以你所描绘的这幅图景似乎是一个充满微妙差别的世界，在这里，美国

sentences.en: States is not fully abandoning its relationship with Europe or France or its allies.
sentences.zh: 并没有完全放弃与欧洲、法国或其盟友的关系。

sentences.en: We're not going to war with some of our longstanding partners, but that it does seem to be that in this new era where the
sentences.zh: 我们不会与某些长期合作伙伴开战，但在这个新时代，似乎美国

sentences.en: United States is almost exclusively focusing its energy on opposing China, that it's asking these allies to come along with them in a very specific way.
sentences.zh: 几乎把全部精力都放在对抗中国上，它正以一种非常具体的方式要求这些盟友一路同行。

sentences.en: And the United States is treating them somewhat more transactionally.
sentences.zh: 而美国对待他们的方式变得更具交易性。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全没错。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of people in Europe that anticipated this.
sentences.zh: 欧洲有很多人预料到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, let's be clear, this has not come as an enormous surprise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，坦白说，这并不是一个巨大的惊喜。

sentences.en: Europeans are good students of the world geopolitical balance.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人很擅长研究世界地缘政治平衡。

sentences.en: I think what surprised them a little bit is how sudden this was.
sentences.zh: 我想让他们有点惊讶的是这一切发生得太突然了。

sentences.en: So remember,
sentences.zh: 所以记住，

sentences.en: President Biden comes into office.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统上任了。

sentences.en: He withdraws from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他从阿富汗撤军。

sentences.en: He doesn't really bother consulting the Brits or the French or the Germans on the timing and logistics of that withdrawal, puts Britain in particular in a very bad spot.
sentences.zh: 他在撤军的时间和后勤问题上并没有真正费心去咨询英国人、法国人或德国人，这让英国人格外陷入了极其尴尬的境地。

sentences.en: They were the second largest NATO contributor of troops to Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他们是北约向阿富汗派遣军队的第二大出兵国。

sentences.en: And he treats them basically like bystanders.
sentences.zh: 而他基本把他们当作旁观者对待。

sentences.en: So that's embarrassing for Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 所以这对鲍里斯·约翰逊来说很尴尬。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson looks like a winner in the submarine deal, but he's clearly a loser in the way he was treated on Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊在潜艇协议中看起来像个赢家，但他在阿富汗问题上的待遇显然是个输家。

sentences.en: And then here we are just a month later, and suddenly it's the
sentences.zh: 然后仅仅过了一个月，我们就到了这里，突然

sentences.en: French that are treated rather casually by the United States.
sentences.zh: 法国人也被美国相当随意地对待了。

sentences.en: So I think what's really surprised and upset people in Europe is they probably expected a president who would invest more time in trying to shore up the alliance.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为真正让欧洲人感到惊讶和不安的是，他们可能期望一位会投入更多时间来试图巩固联盟的总统。

sentences.en: Instead, they got a president who appears to be in a pretty big hurry to tee up his China strategy and
sentences.zh: 相反，他们迎来了这样一位总统：他似乎急于筹备他的对华战略，并且

sentences.en: doesn't mind treating the Europeans fairly roughly in the process of doing that.
sentences.zh: 在这样做的过程中并不介意相当粗鲁地对待欧洲人。

sentences.en: And so really, this is the dawn of the
sentences.zh: 所以真的，这就是

sentences.en: Pacific century of this new era of confrontation and competition between the West and China.
sentences.zh: 太平洋世纪的黎明，这是西方与中国之间对抗与竞争的新时代的黎明。

sentences.en: And these are some of the birth pains of that new age that we're witnessing.
sentences.zh: 我们正在见证这个新时代的阵痛。

sentences.en: Have you trademarked dawn of Pacific century?
sentences.zh: 你给“太平洋世纪的黎明”注册商标了吗？

sentences.en: You should.
sentences.zh: 你应该这么做。

sentences.en: I wish I could say it was mine, but many smarter people have used it before me.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是我想出来的，但在我之前有很多更聪明的人用过它。

sentences.en: Thank you for this, Mark.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，马克。

sentences.en: I really appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thanks, Ested.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，埃斯特德。

sentences.en: Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General, my fellow delegates, to all those who dedicate themselves to this noble mission of this institution,
sentences.zh: 总统先生，秘书长先生，各位代表，所有致力于这个机构这一崇高使命的人们，

sentences.en: it's my honor to speak to you for the first time as President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 很荣幸能首次以美国总统的身份向各位发言。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, in his debut speech to the United Nations General Assembly,
sentences.zh: 周二，在向联合国大会发表的首次演讲中，

sentences.en: President Biden outlined his plan for the United States to reclaim its place as a leader on the global stage.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统概述了他让美国重返全球舞台领导地位的计划。

sentences.en: I stand here today for the first time in 20 years with the United States not at war.
sentences.zh: 今天，我20年来首次站在一个没有处于战争状态的美国面前。

sentences.en: We've turned the page.
sentences.zh: 我们已经翻开了新的一页。

sentences.en: In the speech, Biden argued that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在演讲中，拜登辩称美国

sentences.en: withdrawal from Afghanistan has freed it up to focus on fighting
sentences.zh: 撤出阿富汗使其得以腾出精力专注于打击

sentences.en: America's authoritarian rivals and to promote democracy.
sentences.zh: 美国的威权竞争对手并推广民主。

sentences.en: All the unmatched strength, energy, and commitment, will, and resources of our nation are now fully and squarely focused on what's ahead of us, not what was behind.
sentences.zh: 我们国家无与伦比的力量、活力、承诺、意志和资源现在正全面且直接地聚焦于我们面前的未来，而不是过去。

sentences.en: I know this.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一点。

sentences.en: As we look ahead, we will lead.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，我们将发挥引领作用。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, the House of Representatives passed a bill designed to avert a government
sentences.zh: 周二晚间，众议院通过了一项旨在避免政府

sentences.en: shutdown and a default on American debt by funding government operations through early December and by raising the U.S.
sentences.zh: 关门以及美国债务违约的法案，该法案通过将政府运作资金延长至12月初并提高美国

sentences.en: debt ceiling.
sentences.zh: 债务上限。

sentences.en: But the legislation has little chance of passing in the Senate, where it needs 60 votes and faces strong resistance from Republicans.
sentences.zh: 但该立法在参议院获得通过的可能性很小，在那里它需要60票赞成，并面临来自共和党的强力阻挠。

sentences.en: Unless Congress takes action by September 30th, critical government functions could cease on October 1St.
sentences.zh: 除非国会在9月30日之前采取行动，否则关键的政府职能可能会在10月1日停止。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、妮娜·波塔克和切尔西·丹尼尔制作，穆吉·扎迪提供了帮助。

sentences.zh: 节目由佩姬·考威特和雷切尔·奎斯特剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦贝格和本·兰斯贝格创作。

sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.zh: 本周的《电线切割机秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感而需要全黑环境吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
